Also, can someone with the cards in front of them check to be sure Throat Jab is conditional on doing damage?

It says "the target dealt damage this way", which is a bit less clear than HSA's "Targets dealt damage this way", but probably intended to carry the same meaning.  Spite is still "the target" of Throat Jab, but was not in fact "dealt damage this way", so the wording is a little ambiguous as to intent, but almost certainly is intended to line up with HSA.  (I can't remember what other cards also work like this, apart from Offensive Transmutation which is a near-clone of Throat Jab.  In general, things that entirely stop the target from dealing damage, like TJ and HSA, seem to need to get through, while things that apply a -1 damage penalty, such as Stun Bolt, Hoist Chain and Neurotoxin Dart Thrower, generally work even if entirely blocked.  But there may be exceptions to that pattern - I can't remember whether non-hero cards like Ethereal Bonds and Beat Down follow the same rule as hero cards.)

dpt:

On the other hand, hypersonic assault is useful. Tachyon just needs to hit him some other way, then play Hypersonic Assault.

My Throat Jab will probably be useless forever (serves me right for not looking at what Compound Omicron would do before it came out), but if you can commit to doing HSA on your turn, I have Impromptu Invention in my hand, which will make it possible for me to tutor up a Razor Ordinance and then play Throwing Knives.  I won't dare use two powers on my turn while it results in damage, but once that's been fixed, I can play MCT to go with the other two, and then each turn I can have the Throwing Knives eat his Omicron shield with 1 point getting through (thanks to nemesis), then put Razor Ordinance through his face for 6 (thanks to nemesis again).

Of course, I'll be depending on Visionary to Turmoil the environment deck and protect me from Pervasive Red Dust.  Also if I'm correct in believing she has a second Twist the Ether in hand, playing that on me would be quite nice, as it would let me Throat Jab effectively and then let fly with the Micro-Targeting Barrage for a spectacular 12 damage, plus 1 from the Throat Jab.  Of course, it would be at least as reasonable to play a second TtE on Spite himself, reducing his damage by 2 every time (hooray for TtE not being Limited); this would entirely negate his damage output except for the damage-on-powers stuff, or Mind-Phyre if it somehow finds a lot of Environments in play.  So it might be better for ensuring we win the game, but would make the game feel a bit more lame, and in particular would deprive me of agency.  The decision will be up to Visionary's player, of course; I'm just expressing my wishes for a more gripping and uncertain battle, rather than a boringly effective lockdown.

Ninja city!  I was editing my post to say the same thing while you were posting it.  So which of us ninja'ed the other?  Better ask that funny chap in the police box to sort this one out…

And I agree with Envisioner, we must sacrifice the Good Samaritan, for the greater good.

If I understand the timing correctly, the upshot of this will be that Spite will flip to DWM side, he'll destroy all his non-indestructible cards which consist entirely of the Samaritan, he will heal himself for H because the Samaritan died, then he will heal himself for Hx5 from his advanced text, and only then the Safehouse will deal him 5 damage for each of those it contains.  Right?

If I had retained my Eyepiece, I could have used that (dropping to 11 HP) to determine whether the saving the Samaritan was safe.  But even though Utility Belt is much less useful with me not daring to use powers while Spite can damage me for them, IR Eyepiece is completely worthless (except to draw an extra card each turn) after Spite flips (unlike Turmoil, it can only affect the villain deck).  So I'd be giving up much of my ability to put down Spite if I saved the Samaritan - or saved him this time, if you buy me theory that he's the exact same one that Spite already "killed". (This assumes he just barely survived the turn-1 attack, and then Visi wiped his memory of meeting Spite while also controlling Spite's mind to make him Lab Raid again, leaving the Samaritan to repeat the entire incident and be killed in the same way, if Wraith doesn't prevent this.  I kind of want to work this entire funny scenario into my story, but it requires me to somehow acknowledge the very game-mechanical decision of which equipment to let the Red Dust perma-destroy and which one to salvage from its effects, and I haven't been able to figure out a way of translating that into setting-reality terms.)
